findings.title: read_timeout is per-read; no overall deadline bounds the request
findings.evidence: read_timeout is passed to Net::HTTP.start, which applies it per socket read, not to the whole response; a server that sends one byte just under every 5s keeps the call (and the calling thread) alive indefinitely, and retries multiply that.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the request in a hard deadline (e.g. Timeout.timeout with a total budget covering open + read + retries, or use Net::HTTP's read loop with a deadline check) and document the total worst-case duration.

findings.title: Net::HTTP internal max_retries doubles the intended attempt count
findings.evidence: Net::HTTP.start defaults to max_retries = 1 and silently retries idempotent requests on connection resets, so MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3 can become up to 6 transport attempts and roughly double the worst-case wall time/backoff.
findings.recommendation: Pass max_retries: 0 in the Net::HTTP.start keyword arguments so the only retry policy is the explicit one in this method.

findings.title: Common transient transport errors are not retried
findings.evidence: The retryable list covers only open/read timeouts and ECONNRESET, so Errno::ETIMEDOUT, Errno::EHOSTUNREACH, EOFError, SocketError and OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError abort the fetch immediately despite the documented transient-error retry.
findings.recommendation: Add the other transient classes (Errno::ETIMEDOUT, Errno::EHOSTUNREACH, EOFError, SocketError, OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError, IOError) to RETRYABLE_ERRORS, and consider retrying 429/5xx responses with backoff.

findings.title: Response body is read fully with no size cap
findings.evidence: response.body buffers the entire response in memory and no Content-Length/max-size check exists, so an unexpectedly large body can exhaust process memory.
findings.recommendation: Enforce a maximum body size (check Content-Length before reading and/or stream with read_body, aborting past a configured cap) and raise a distinct error when exceeded.

findings.title: Non-success status raises a bare RuntimeError with the status discarded
findings.evidence: The non-success branch raises an untyped RuntimeError built from a string, so callers cannot rescue a specific error class or inspect code/headers, and diagnostics (status code, body) are lost.
findings.recommendation: Define a dedicated error class (e.g. HttpFetch::Error / HTTPStatusError) that carries response.code and body, and raise that instead of a string exception.

findings.title: Host is never validated after the scheme check
findings.evidence: Only the URI class is checked; a value such as the string 'https:foo' parses as URI::HTTPS with a nil host, producing a confusing downstream failure from Net::HTTP.start rather than a clear ArgumentError.
findings.recommendation: Also reject when uri.host is nil/empty (and optionally reject userinfo) with a clear ArgumentError before starting the request.

findings.title: Retry/timeout behaviour has no tests
findings.evidence: No test commands were run and no test files are in the diff, so the retry bound, backoff and https-only guard are unverified; a broken counter or a non-retried transient error would go unnoticed.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests stubbing Net::HTTP.start to assert: non-https raises ArgumentError, success returns the body, a retryable error retries exactly MAX_ATTEMPTS times then re-raises, and a non-retryable error propagates immediately.
